title: How AI Trading Scams Make Real Results Look Bad
description:
Want to copy my algo trades without installing bots or running a VPS?
https://copy.responsibleforextrading.com/

Website: https://responsibleforextrading.com/

AI trading scams don’t just cost people money—they can make real trading results look disappointing. When an AI trading bot supposedly earns thousands every day, what happens to our expectations of legitimate trading?

In this video, I examine how exaggerated promises and crypto trading bot scam tutorials can distort what traders consider believable. I also share my own experience losing money after following one of these tutorials—and explain why a convincing video, positive comments and impressive screenshots aren’t enough to establish trust.

Whether you’re exploring AI for forex trading, researching forex robots or watching an AI trading bot review, these are three questions worth asking:

• Who can move or withdraw your money?
• What do the results actually show: live trading, a demo or a backtest?
• What risk was taken to produce those returns?

A profitable screenshot doesn’t establish a reliable strategy. Smaller returns don’t automatically make someone trustworthy either. Every claim deserves scrutiny—including mine.

This applies whether you’re considering a crypto bot, an MT5 trading bot or an AI forex trading bot. The goal is to understand the evidence before trusting the promises.

Have these videos changed what you expect from trading bots—or made you more skeptical of all of them? Share your experience in the comments.

ABOUT ME
I’m Ryan Brown, founder of Responsible Forex Trading. I’ve been trading since 2005 and developing algorithmic trading strategies since around 2015.



DISCLOSURE
I develop and sell trading software. Apply the same scrutiny to my results and claims as you would to anyone else’s.

For educational purposes only, not personalized financial advice. Trading involves risk, and past performance does not guarantee future results.
